The King did what the vizier had advised, and before six months had passed, all the cats
that were in that city had perished. That group of people went by
and after them another grew up hating cats: every time
they noticed a slight corruption caused by mice, in some garment, furniture, or food,
they said, ‘Look Could a cat have gone through the city?’Also,
whenever it so happened that people or animals got inflicted by a disease, they said,
‘It almost seems as if some cat passed through the city.’ With this trick
the rats rid themselves of the horror of the cats and were at peace from them. And if this
weak and lowly living being could conceive of such trickery, so as to
get rid of his enemy, then hope must not be lost in man, who is
the smartest and wisest living being, can obtain from his enemy what he wants using his ingenuity.
The Chapter of the Rat and Cat

p.n: The King Asks about Escaping Enemies

body.p:
“I have understood this parable,” said King Dayshalīm to the Philosopher Baydanā. “Now tell
me a parable about a man who was weak and his enemies were many and, blocking him from every side, put him on the brink
of perishing, so he sought reconciliation with one of his enemies, thereby becoming safe, then kept his promise to the one with whom
he had reconciled. So tell me about the nature of truce-how it should be sought.”
